source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting excessive industrial emissions in an air-quality report

1. Start with the monitoring records.
2.
completion:
Analyze the data collected to identify periods showing unusually high levels of emissions.
3. Compare the observed emissions against permit limits set by the regulatory authority.
4. Note both the severity and frequency of the excessive emissions.
5. Include time-stamped photographic or visual evidence if available.
6. Document meteorological conditions during episodes of high emissions to assess their potential impact.
7. Provide methods and instruments used for monitoring, including calibration records and maintenance logs of the equipment.
8. Record any operational anomalies, maintenance activities, or upsets that coincide with high emissions episodes.
9. Include any communication or correspondence with the facility regarding observed emissions.
10. Summarize the data, noting trends, patterns, and areas for further investigation.
11. Cross-reference with any local or national emissions inventory data to provide context.
12. Highlight any violations of air quality standards or regulations.
13. Use specific units and emission factors to quantify the excess pollution.
14. Include recommendations
